purpose_of_this_fixture: A strong discovery call that follows the method. The Consultant opens with connection, frames the call as a conversation with an honest-expert line, and walks through the current state. Pains are excavated in the client's own words, including why the workaround will not do. Why now is clear: the Des Moines office opens November 2, and the Larkspur Falls pursuit was lost in July over a missed deadline. The client calculates and confirms a bleed, gives an upside with a 'what would you go after' answer, and describes the desired outcome. The decision process is mapped (the managing partner signs spend over $25k and was not on the call), followed by priority, blockers, a first-cut scope playback and a dated next step. It tests that the plugin (1) grades R1-R10 Met from client-side verbatim quotes, R11 Missing (no demo yet) and R12 Partial, giving the verdict 'Discovery complete' with the proposal gate still closed; (2) grades per-pain checks with realistic gaps (P3 Reach Partial and Trajectory Missing; P4 not excavated); (3) keeps the bleed at the client's own total, leaves unquantified items out of it (write-off share, principals' time, the $38k write-off, the lost $1.4M fee) and keeps loaded rates apart from bill rates; (4) picks up client vocabulary (pursuits, fee proposals, jobs, phases, submittals, the Wall, owner); (5) treats the Ajera connection as a must-have while asking about hosting, access and data direction instead of assuming; (6) turns the polite hedge on full go-live and the modelling traps (one project with several jobs, phases that vary by job type) into questions; and (7) proposes a CRM plus Work Management blueprint and a first build.
transcript_format: Plain text, 242 lines, one speaker turn per line in the form '[HH:MM:SS] Speaker Name: text'. Timestamps are turn start times from [00:00:04] to [00:45:02]. No header lines and no call date. Three speakers: 'Consultant', 'Tess Kowalczyk' (COO) and 'Jordan Pruitt' (Operations Manager). About 5,730 spoken words (about 6,370 including timestamps and labels). Client talk share is about 74% (Tess 44%, Jordan 29%); the Consultant's longest turn is 89 words at [00:40:02]. Non-verbal cues appear in square brackets ([laughs], [sighs], [muffled]); interruptions and self-corrections use ' -- '. ASCII only. The weekday-date pairs mentioned (Tuesday the fifteenth, Friday the eighteenth, Thursday the twenty-fourth, the first Thursday being October first) fit a call in September 2026, before Tuesday 15 September; the exact call date is not stated. Every location in this key is 'HH:MM:SS Speaker Name (role)', taken from the line the quote is on.

rubric.note: The client walks through three flows end to end. Pursuits: intake, the pursuit log, the Friday huddle and go/no-go, the fee builder, Gordon's fee sign-off, submission, short list and interview, job setup in Ajera. Delivery: phases, weekly time entry in Ajera, the Wall, the Tuesday staffing call, the monthly WIP report and PM burn sheets. CA: submittals via Procore or email, the Excel submittal log, Bluebeam, and owner sign-off letters by email. Tools and their lack of connections are named. People and time: Hallie about 10 h/wk; Jordan 'most of Monday and half of Tuesday morning' (costed at 12 h/wk); a 12-person staffing call that runs an hour; PMs about 3 h/wk each; 20 minutes to an hour per Ajera export. monday today is Anneke's free FF and E board, lapsed and unused. Thin areas to list as assumptions: how owner approvals are tracked ('The PMs track it however they track it'), where owner (client) contacts live (never discussed), how the fee builder is structured, and Ajera hosting and access.

entities_and_workflows: Pursuit intake: RFQs and RFPs from public bid portals or a PIC's relationships reach Hallie (marketing coordinator), who logs them in the Excel pursuit log on SharePoint
Friday pursuit huddle (meant to take 30 minutes): review new pursuits and decide go/no-go; on a go, a PIC and a PM are assigned

Fee proposal: the PM builds the fee in the fee builder (hours by phase and discipline times rates); Hallie assembles quals, resumes and project sheets; Gordon (managing partner) signs off every fee proposal; then it is submitted
Addenda are issued on the bid portal to registered contacts only and can move the due date
After submission: short list, interview, won or lost. Today 6-7 fee proposals a month; the plan is 10 once Des Moines is up
A won pursuit becomes a job: Bev (controller) sets it up in Ajera with a job number and phases by reading the fee proposal PDF and retyping it
A project can contain several Ajera jobs (the Oak Street fire station is a base-building job plus an apparatus bay equipment package as an additional service)
Job phases: SD, DD, CDs, bidding and CA, each with its own fee; engineering-only jobs may have only design and CA
Weekly time entry in Ajera against job and phase (stays in Ajera)

Fee burn: Bev's monthly WIP report after billing close (around the 10th-12th of the following month); some PMs keep weekly burn sheets from an Ajera export and a VLOOKUP; write-offs were about $210k last fiscal year

Staffing: PMs are meant to update allocations. Jordan rebuilds the Wall (a tab per office, people by week, percentages) on Monday and Tuesday morning from Teams messages, project schedules and Ajera hours. The Tuesday 1 p.m. staffing call has about 12 people.

CA submittals arrive from GCs via Procore (about half) or as emailed PDFs. The PM logs them in a per-job Excel submittal log, and the reviewer marks them up and stamps them in Bluebeam. Review windows are ten business days or 14 calendar days, depending on the contract.
Owner approvals: SD and DD packages go out by email with a sign-off letter; signed letters come back, or work continues without them

Offices: Madison (main), Milwaukee and Rockford. Des Moines opens November 2 with 4 people (a PIC, two designers, a marketing hire) and should reach about 15 within two years. Staffing crosses offices (two light Rockford engineers could have helped Milwaukee).
Healthcare pursuits: 2-3 a quarter declined for lack of capacity; fees $400k-$600k; hit rate about 1 in 4

Buying process for this purchase: Tess owns the budget; Gordon signs over $25k; Bev must be comfortable with anything touching Ajera; Marcus runs an IT checklist; the partner meeting agenda (first Thursday; next October 1, when the budget locks). Then a PO or card payment, and rollout by Tess and Jordan.
